content.user_title: Organize Project Files With Clear Structure
content.value_statement: Growing projects often become hard to navigate when folders and names evolve without rules. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical structures for cleaner codebases.
actual_capabilities: Suggests folder structures for React and Next.js applications.
Suggests layered structures for Node.js and Express backends.
Explains feature-based organization for larger applications.
Defines file, folder, function, component, and constant naming rules.
Shows when to use index.ts barrel files and when to avoid broad exports.
Recommends path alias patterns for cleaner imports.
limitations: It provides organization guidance but does not analyze runtime dependencies automatically.
It does not migrate files unless the host agent is asked to make edits.
It focuses on TypeScript web projects more than mobile, data, or infrastructure repositories.
It cannot replace team review for domain-specific module boundaries.

use_cases.title: Structure a New Web Application
use_cases.description: Create a clear starting layout for a React, Next.js, or full-stack TypeScript project.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Growing Backend
use_cases.description: Separate routes, controllers, services, repositories, models, and tests into maintainable backend layers.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Naming Rules
use_cases.description: Define consistent file, folder, type, hook, component, and test naming rules for shared repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new project layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose a folder structure for a new TypeScript React project with components, hooks, utilities, tests, and configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Folders
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my current project tree and suggest a cleaner folder structure with naming conventions and migration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Feature Modules
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a large application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a feature-based structure for authentication, products, orders, shared UI, state, API clients, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Define Team Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create repository organization standards for folders, file names, barrel exports, path aliases, and maximum nesting depth.

output_examples.input: A small Next.js app needs clearer folders for UI, routes, utilities, and types.
output: A proposed structure separates app routes, reusable UI, layout components, utilities, types, configuration, and tests.
The guidance recommends consistent naming and clear import paths for shared modules.

output_examples.input: An Express backend has routes, models, and business logic mixed together.
output: A layered structure separates API routes, controllers, services, repositories, models, middleware, database files, utilities, and tests.
The recommendation explains ownership for each layer and reduces circular dependency risk.

output_examples.input: A team wants rules for component files, hooks, constants, and tests.
output: The skill provides naming standards for components, hooks, utilities, constants, types, tests, folders, and private members.
It also recommends keeping related component files, styles, and tests close together.

best_practices: Choose one naming convention per repository and document it before files multiply.
Keep related component files, tests, styles, and types close when they change together.
Use feature boundaries for large applications and shared folders only for truly reusable code.
anti_patterns: Do not create vague folders such as misc, helpers, or utils2 without clear ownership.
Do not add deep nesting when a flatter structure would still show intent.
Do not export everything through barrel files when explicit exports improve clarity and tree shaking.

faq.question: Does this skill move files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides structure and naming guidance. A host agent can apply changes only when you explicitly request edits.

faq.question: Which project types does it support best?
faq.answer: It fits React, Next.js, Node.js, Express, and TypeScript web projects best.

faq.question: Can it help with an existing messy repository?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current project tree and ask for a proposed structure with migration notes.

faq.question: Does it define naming conventions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers components, hooks, utilities, constants, types, tests, folders, and private members.

faq.question: Can teams use it for standards documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft repository standards for folder roles, names, exports, aliases, and nesting depth.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It mainly covers maintainability. It also discourages circular dependencies and unclear shared folders.
